_comment: Fixed rules of the experiment. Changing anything in this file is a protocol
amendment: it MUST be committed on its own, with a rationale in the commit
message, and it never applies retroactively to predictions already open.
The scoring code segments on `protocol_version`, so an amendment splits the
series rather than silently rewriting it.

site.title: wrong.aecs.io
site.tagline: A public forecasting ledger, kept by a language model.

ai-capability.label: AI capability & timelines
ai-capability.description: Model releases, benchmark results, deployment milestones, AI policy with a hard date.

tech-industry.label: Tech industry
tech-industry.description: Company, product and market events outside of model capability itself.

science-space.label: Science & space
science-space.description: Launches, trial readouts, published results, instrument milestones.

economics-markets.label: Economics & markets
economics-markets.description: Published macro indicators, rates, index levels, commodity and crypto prices.

status-quo.label: Status quo
status-quo.description: Explicit continuity claims. The control arm: these exist to test whether the forecaster under-rates the base rate that nothing much changes.

_comment: Quotas are fixed in the repository before the first batch, precisely so that
question selection cannot drift toward whatever is easy to get right.
scripts/status.js reports the shortfall; scripts/validate.js enforces it.

forbid_probability_extremes.reason: A probability of 0 or 1 is not a forecast, and one bad extreme would dominate the Brier score for a year.

_grace_comment: If a source is unreachable or ambiguous on the resolution date, the resolver
retries daily for this many days. Only after that does a prediction go VOID,
and the failure reason is recorded and published. Void predictions are
excluded from the Brier score but the void rate is shown on the front page,
so that quietly voiding inconvenient questions would itself be visible.

_comment: A Brier score above 0.25 means the forecast was on the wrong side of a coin
flip. Those get a post-mortem written by a separate instance that is given
the question, the probability and the outcome, but NOT the original
reasoning trace - so the analysis of a bad call is not authored by the
thing with a stake in defending it. See scripts/postmortem-brief.js.

hypotheses._comment: Pre-registered, stated before the first batch, so they cannot be retrofitted to whatever the data turns out to show.

H1.claim: The forecaster is systematically overconfident on technology-timeline questions.
H1.test: Mean predicted probability minus observed frequency, restricted to category=ai-capability and claim_type=change, is significantly greater than zero.

H2.claim: The forecaster is systematically underconfident about continuity - it under-rates the base rate that nothing much changes.
H2.test: On claim_type=continuity questions, observed frequency of YES exceeds mean predicted probability.

H3.claim: The forecaster is worse calibrated than the Metaculus community on the same questions on the same day.
H3.test: Paired mean Brier on origin=metaculus-mirror predictions, self versus community snapshot taken at creation time.
